column1: # readiness.tsv — the ATTESTATION TABLE read by conformance/readiness.sh.
# Nine conditional readiness checks used to be nine files implementing one shape: detect a SURFACE
# (data / deploy / AI / agent / sensitive data); if it is absent render N/A; if it is present require
# a RECORD LINE in a named artifact and require its template PLACEHOLDER to be gone. The shape lives
# in conformance/readiness.sh; the policy lives here.
# THE THREE-STATE CONTRACT IS UNCHANGED and is the whole point: N/A (no surface — the check declined
# and said so) · OK (the record is present and filled) · FAIL (record missing, or still holding its
# placeholder). rc is 0 for N/A and OK, 1 for FAIL, 2 only for usage. A green run proves a posture
# was RECORDED — never that the recorded thing is true, tested, or works. Each case's own honest
# ceiling is carried verbatim in its `ok` text.
# DIRECTIONAL SAFETY: detection ESCALATES, it never EXEMPTS. Every trigger is deliberately
# conservative, so a MISS means "not nagged", never "exempted" — the matching conformance/*-readiness.md
# checklist is the gate of record and a human applies it regardless.
# FORMAT — TWELVE tab-separated fields per data line; `-` means "not applicable to this row".
# `#` comments and blank lines are skipped. `{}` in any text is substituted (see below).
#   1 case          the check name: `sh conformance/readiness.sh <case> [project-dir]`
#   2 kind          case | file | line | absent
#   3 id            file rows DEFINE an id; line/absent rows REFER to one. `-` on case rows.
#   4 a             case: the trigger predicate (conformance/surface-lib.sh; `pred:arg` passes arg)
#                   file: SPACE-separated candidate paths, first existing one wins
#   5 b             case: the N/A text (`\n` = a further line)   line: the record-line regex
#                                                                absent: the regex that must NOT appear
#   6 c             case: the OK text                            line: the placeholder regex, or `-`
#   7 d             line: a regex the record line must ALSO match, or `-`
#   8 fail-missing  file: text when no candidate exists · line: text when the record line is absent
#                   (`-` on a line row means this row only judges an EXISTING line)
#   9 fail-reject   line/absent: text when the placeholder/forbidden regex matches
#  10 fail-require  line: text when field 7 does not match
#  11 sample-good   the --selftest fixture cell: file rows = seed content · line rows = a conforming line
#  12 sample-bad    the --selftest mutant cell: a line that trips field 6, 7 or (absent) field 5
# `{}` SUBSTITUTION — one token, and its meaning is positional exactly as the retired checks' `$dir`
# / `$plan` / `$card` were: on a `case` N/A text and a `file` fail text it is the PROJECT DIR; on a
# `line`/`absent` text it is the RESOLVED FILE PATH. Texts with no `{}` are emitted verbatim.
# ALL greps are POSIX ERE and CASE-INSENSITIVE (grep -Eiq), matching every retired check's own flags.
# --selftest generates, per case: a no-surface fixture (must render N/A) · a filled fixture (must
# render OK) · one mutant per `file` row (delete the file) · one per `line` row with a fail-missing
# text (delete the record line) · one per row with a sample-bad (plant it). Each mutant must go RED
# with THAT ROW'S text, so a row that cannot be killed is a row that is not really enforced.
# ── agentops-ready (MP-3a) — an AGENTIC project records its agent-run trace discipline.
agentops-ready
